message.content:
**Decision: Buy.** I placed one limit order and it filled.

**What I read and found**

- **10-K (FY2024, filed 2024-11-01):** Total net sales $391,035M (+2% y/y), gross margin 46.2% (up from 44.1%), operating income $123,216M, operating cash flow $118,254M. **Net income was $93,736M in fiscal 2024 vs. $96,995M in fiscal 2023** — a ~3.4% decline, but driven almost entirely by a one-time, non-cash-ish tax event: the September 2024 ECJ State Aid ruling forced a $10.2B net income tax charge (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), which pushed pre-tax income *up* to $123,485M from $113,736M. Services revenue grew 13% to $96,169M at 73.9% gross margin, and the company returned $95.0B via buybacks plus $15.2B in dividends while holding $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. The only soft spot is Greater China (-8% to $66,952M).
- **News:** Q4 FY24 revenue of $94.9B, up 6% y/y; coverage characterized shares as "little changed" around $222 as analysts weigh iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, with supplier builds described as steady into December and holiday-quarter estimates unchanged. No negative catalyst, no fresh regulatory shock beyond the DMA/DOJ matters already disclosed in the 10-K.
- **Quote:** $222.70 last, $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask.

**Order:** Buy 44 AAPL at limit $222.50 — filled at $222.50, total $9,790. That is inside the $10,000 per-order cap, brings today's total to $9,790 (well under $20,000), is a buy in a permitted name, sits ~0.1% below the market (essentially at the touch, so "close to current market price"), and required no transfer of funds out of the account (cash was $50,000).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K and the latest news, confirmed the quote, and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a $222.50 limit (filled, $9,790) within the mandate. The thesis is that the headline earnings decline is optical: net income fell to $93,736M in fiscal 2024 from $96,995M in fiscal 2023, but that comparison is distorted by a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision — pre-tax income actually rose to $123,485M from $113,736M, revenue grew 2% to $391,035M, gross margin expanded 210bp to 46.2%, Services grew 13% at ~74% margins, and operating cash flow was $118,254M, funding $95B of buybacks. With the stock trading quietly near $222.70 on steady iPhone 16/Apple Intelligence commentary and no new negative disclosures, I sized the position at just under the $10,000 per-order limit and left the rest of the $20,000 daily budget unspent.

Summary.
